## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet, and the starting architecture scored 0.000 on both seeds. With the default recipe the budget gives only about 131k steps, or 32 PPO updates. Exact builds are rare, so success may depend on how many samples and updates the budget allows, and on whether the network can tell which layer a brick will land on. The starting network merges all layers into one 2D feature map. To place a brick correctly it must work out the highest filled cell under the footprint and compare that layer with the target, which is hard to learn. I'm testing two factors in a small grid: (1) a recipe with more samples and more updates (2 PPO epochs, smaller updates) on the starting architecture; (2) a new layer-aware head that scores each brick at each candidate layer and takes a soft maximum over layers, with both the default recipe and the faster recipe.

### Round 2
All six training runs scored exactly 0, both on dev and on training designs in the last 10% of training. That held for two architectures (a 3x3 conv net and a per-layer footprint net) and two recipes (4 epochs, and 2 epochs with about 1.8 times the samples). The reward gives credit for every correct cell, so near-zero learning that is identical across all of these suggests a structural mismatch rather than slow learning. The task warns that the world may differ from its description. Both networks assume the action index maps to the described cell, brick type and corner, with DONE as the last action. If the indexing is transposed, anchored at another corner, uses swapped footprints or puts DONE elsewhere, a head tied to cell positions cannot learn it. Test: add a learned linear head over all actions, fed by flattened per-cell features. It can learn any action mapping.

### Round 3
All 6 trials scored 0 on both seeds, and training success was also 0. That held across conv and per-layer networks, 1 to 4 PPO epochs and up to 390k steps, so the networks are failing to learn at all, not falling short on generalisation. The task warns that the world may differ from its description. Three explanations fit the evidence. First, the action layout may not match the observation grid (for example, transposed or anchored differently); every head so far assumes it does. Second, the agent may be collapsing to DONE: random placements mostly earn negative reward, and DONE ends the episode at 0. Third, the per-layer net's assumed channel grouping may simply be wrong. The free linear head should have handled a layout mismatch in principle, but it probably learns too slowly. This round therefore tests:
- layout-robust heads that also take the action mask as input;
- a fully connected net with no layout assumptions;
- an exploration-heavy recipe on the starting network.

### Round 4
All nine trials scored exactly 0 on dev and 0 on training success. That held across the starting conv net, per-layer footprint nets, free linear heads, a mask-input transposed head, an exploration recipe, and a plain MLP. Seed noise cannot explain this: no idea has produced any signal. The starting net's 1x1 stem already learns its channel mixing, and a 5x5 receptive field allows small anchor shifts, so channel order is unlikely to be the blocker. Three explanations are still open. The action layout might be type-minor, which no trial has tested. The policy might stay too uniform, because raising entropy failed but lowering it was never tried. Or the agent might simply need more samples. In this last round each bet targets a different untested explanation, because any score above 0 would beat the start.
